warnings.breastfeeding: Extra caution is needed because nursing Mothers A breastfed infant with G6PD deficiency is at risk for hemolytic anemia from exposure to primaquine.
warnings.kidney: Kidney function can influence clearance; nephrology input may be required for advanced renal impairment.
warnings.liver: Hepatic impairment may require dose changes and periodic liver function monitoring.
warnings.alcohol: Alcohol may amplify sedation or liver stress; avoid unless your clinician approves.

faqs.question: Can I rely on this Primaquine phosphate information instead of a doctor visit?
faqs.answer: No. This content supports learning and preparation for conversations with qualified healthcare professionals. It is not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment.

faqs.question: Can I adjust the dose of Primaquine phosphate on my own?
faqs.answer: Dose changes should only be made with clinician guidance. Self-adjustment can increase side effects or reduce effectiveness.
